# Alamut

> Alamut is a free browser app for playing and learning a Gear4music DISC 10-note D Kurd handpan. It has 3 patterns with number notation, a 3D handpan that plays by tap, keyboard or phone motion, microphone note detection, and bar-by-bar practice. The interface is in English and Persian.

The instrument has ten notes: D3 (ding), 146.8 Hz; A3, 220.0 Hz; B♭3, 233.1 Hz; C4, 261.6 Hz; D4, 293.7 Hz; E4, 329.6 Hz; F4, 349.2 Hz; G4, 392.0 Hz; A4, 440.0 Hz; C5, 523.3 Hz. Number notation maps 0 to the ding and 1 to 9 to the tone fields from low A3 to high C5. Songs from other keys are transposed so that every note lands on these ten; the pages say which notes were substituted.

## Pages

- [The app](https://handpan.moshes.io/): library, Play and Learn. Piece routes are /#/p/<id>, /#/p/<id>/play and /#/p/<id>/learn
- [All pieces](https://handpan.moshes.io/p/): every pattern with notation, grouped by kind
- [Features and limits](https://handpan.moshes.io/features): what the app does today
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/m-esm/handpan): the code, piece data and checks

## Songs

Riffs and melodies from well-known songs, moved onto the pan's ten notes.

- [In the End](https://handpan.moshes.io/p/in-the-end): Linkin Park's piano riff moved down to D minor, over D minor, C and B-flat. 105 BPM, 4/4, 39 bars.
- [Seven Nation Army](https://handpan.moshes.io/p/seven-nation-army): The White Stripes riff in D minor: 4 4 6 4 3 2 1, then the ding joins for the chorus. 124 BPM, 4/4, 16 bars.
- [Nothing Else Matters (Intro)](https://handpan.moshes.io/p/nothing-else-matters): Metallica's intro as the picking part in A minor, for playing with a guitarist on capo 5. 48 BPM, 6/8, 28 bars.

## Optional
